finding: Deleting a page silently re-points every internal link that targeted it at the home page: the inspector writes internal links as `#page:<pageId>`, and the exporter's fallback for an unresolvable id is index.html — no warning at delete, no issue raised, no reverse index anywhere.
evidence: LinkSection.tsx:191 writes `#page:${pageId}`; ExportEngine.ts:801-803 `resolveHref` returns `this.pageHrefs.get(...) ?? "index.html"`, with its own comment 'a page deleted after the link was made — falls back to the home page'. PageManager.ts:254-276 deletePage unregisters the route and deletes the element subtree and touches no other page's links. Grep for '#page:' across packages/editor/src returns 6 hits (ExportEngine 753/801/802/1030, LinkSection 114/116/191) — no validator, no issues check, no delete-time scan.
fix: Before confirming a page delete, walk every other page's element tree for `href` starting `#page:<id>` and name the count in the ConfirmDialog ('3 links on 2 pages point here'). Offer to re-target or clear them. Failing that, at minimum emit a PROJECT_CHANGED-visible warning and raise an Issues row instead of resolving to index.html at export time.
chain: Pages -> PageData -> deletePage -> (no event scans element hrefs) -> Inspector/LinkSection + ExportEngine -> every inbound internal link silently navigates to the home page on the published site

finding: PAGE_RECOVERED is emitted by the one code path that DESTROYS a page's content and nothing listens to it: RecoveryManager replaces a page whose root element is missing with a fresh empty container, tells nobody, records no history entry, and the next autosave persists the empty page.
evidence: RecoveryManager.ts:168-197 `ensurePageRootExists` builds `newRootData` with `children: []`, assigns `page.root = newRootData`, then `this.composer.emit(EVENTS.PAGE_RECOVERED, { page })`. Grep for EVENTS.PAGE_RECOVERED across packages/editor/src returns exactly one hit — that emit. No `composer.on(EVENTS.PAGE_RECOVERED` anywhere. It is reached from `recoverFromInactivity` (:148-150) and `validateAllPages` (:212), i.e. on an inactivity timer, unattended.
fix: Listen for PAGE_RECOVERED in the shell: raise a persistent (duration 0) toast naming the page, force a history checkpoint BEFORE the root swap (`composer.history.forceCheckpoint('before recovery')`, HistoryManager.ts:360) so ⌘Z is real, and suppress autosave until the user acknowledges. A recovery that cannot be seen is a silent delete.
chain: Pages -> PageData.root -> RecoveryManager.ensurePageRootExists -> emits PAGE_RECOVERED -> nobody -> page content replaced by an empty div and autosaved over the real content

finding: '+ Add page' can mint a page whose name AND slug already exist, and the DB has a unique index on (siteId, slug) — so from that moment every autosave of the whole project fails with an unmapped 500.
evidence: getDefaultPageName (shared/utils/pageUtils.ts:16-20) names by COUNT: `return \`Page ${count + 1}\``. usePages.ts:176-178 calls it and derives `slug = slugify(name)`. PageManager.createPage (:61-92) does no name or slug uniqueness check (contrast duplicatePage :309-310, which uses uniqueCopyName/uniqueCopySlug against existingNames()/existingSlugs()). Walk: Home, About, Page 3, Page 4 -> delete 'Page 3' -> count is 3 -> next add is named 'Page 4', slug 'page-4', which already exists. prisma/schema.prisma:597 `@@unique([siteId, slug])`. sites.ts router :271-298 maps only SITE_NOT_FOUND / EMPTY_SNAPSHOT / SAVE_CONFLICT — a Prisma P2002 rethrows as a generic INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.
fix: Make createPage resolve collisions the way duplicatePage already does (reuse existingNames/existingSlugs), and have getDefaultPageName take the existing names rather than a count. Separately, map P2002 on pages.slug in sites.saveProject to a CONFLICT naming the two pages, so the failure is legible instead of a repeating 500.
chain: Pages -> PageData.slug -> addPage -> (no uniqueness check) -> sites.saveProject -> Prisma @@unique([siteId,slug]) -> every autosave 500s until the user finds and renames the duplicate

finding: Switching pages pushes an undo entry, because the snapshot the history diffs against always differs: exportProject() stamps a fresh metadata.updatedAt on every call, so isPatchEmpty never fires. The guard written for exactly this — isNavigationOnlyChange — is used by the dirty markers and NOT by HistoryManager.
evidence: PageManager.setActivePage:225-231 emits PROJECT_CHANGED `{ type: "page:activated" }`. HistoryManager.ts:93-125 `projectChangedHandler` does not inspect the payload type; after coalesceDelay (500ms, :84) it calls record(). record() (:191-204) diffs `captureSnapshot()` against `getCurrentState()`; captureSnapshot is `deepClone(this.composer.exportProject())` (:378) and Composer.exportProject:603-616 sets `updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()` at :611. JsonPatch.createPatch (:40) has no field exclusions, so the patch always carries `replace /metadata/updatedAt` and `isPatchEmpty` (:311) is always false. events.ts:695-702 isNavigationOnlyChange exists; its only consumer is useDirtyPages.ts:59.
fix: Have HistoryManager's projectChangedHandler skip payloads passing isNavigationOnlyChange, and exclude `metadata.updatedAt` from the diff (or stop stamping it inside exportProject and set it at the save boundary instead) so isPatchEmpty can do the job it was written for.
chain: Pages -> active page -> setActivePage emits PROJECT_CHANGED(page:activated) -> HistoryManager records a non-empty patch -> user presses ⌘Z after browsing pages and nothing visible happens

finding: A slug change on a published page records slugHistory and produces no redirect anywhere in the product: nothing reads Page.slugHistory, the Redirect table is only ever written by the dashboard's manual form, and the site-level slug_history table is written and read by nobody.
evidence: PageManager.updatePage:130-144 pushes `{ slug: oldSlug, changedAt }` onto page.slugHistory (docstring at :13 promises '90-day redirect export'). Grep for slugHistory across server/, lib/, packages/editor/src: every hit is a persist or a type — no consumer. server/services/redirect.service.ts:26 `prisma.redirect.create` is reached only from site-detail.ts:94-109 (the manual Redirects screen). server/services/site-settings.service.ts:191 `prisma.slugHistory.create` is the ONLY reference to that table in the whole repo — no read. The editor's own warning copy admits it: SeoTab.tsx:296-297 'Consider setting up a redirect in your hosting settings after saving.'
fix: On publish, turn each page's slugHistory into Redirect rows (fromPath = /<oldSlug>.html, toUrl = the page's current path, 301) — or emit them into the deploy as a Vercel routes config in lib/publish-files.ts, where robots.txt and sitemap.xml are already assembled. Either way the warning stops asking the user to do it by hand in a place the product owns.
chain: Pages -> PageData.slugHistory -> updatePage(slug) -> (no consumer) -> Publish / Redirects -> the old URL 404s and the recorded history is dead weight

finding: The slug-change warning gate is FIXED but half-blind within a session: it now reads projectMetadata.publishedUrl, which is only ever written by the load path — no code anywhere sets it after a publish, so a user who publishes and then edits a slug in the same session still gets no warning.
evidence: usePageSettings.ts:361 `const publishedUrl = composer?.getProjectMetadata?.()?.publishedUrl ?? null`, gating SeoTab.tsx:289 `s.slug !== page.slug && !!s.publishedUrl && !s.slugError`. The prior `page.status === 'live'` gate is gone (types/project.ts:75 documents why). The only writer of that field is BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:335, inside loadProject's return. `setProjectMetadata` does not exist; Composer.updateProjectMetadata (:785) and mergeProjectMetadata (:805) exist and are never called with publishedUrl (grep: zero hits). AquibraStudio.tsx:446 emits SITE_PUBLISHED on a real publish and the only listener is OnboardingMount.tsx:64.
fix: Add a SITE_PUBLISHED listener that calls composer.mergeProjectMetadata({ publishedUrl: url }) — the merge variant, so a publish does not mark the project dirty. One listener closes the gap for the slug warning, copyPageLink and anything else that asks 'is this site reachable'.
chain: Publish -> SITE_PUBLISHED -> (only onboarding listens) -> Pages/page-settings -> publishedUrl stays null until reload -> the destructive slug warning stays silent on a site that IS live

finding: slugHistory is persisted in three mutually incompatible shapes — the writer's, the editor's own validation schema's, and the server's declared type — so any consumer written against one of them would be wrong about the other two.
evidence: Writer: PageManager.ts:136 pushes `{ slug: oldSlug, changedAt: ... }` (matches shared/types/project.ts:182-187 SlugChange, and packages/shared/schemas/sites.ts:140-145 slugHistorySchema). Editor's ProjectDataSchema: packages/editor/src/shared/schemas/project.ts:30 requires `z.object({ slug, timestamp })` — a field that is never written; that schema is the collaboration import gate (CollaborationManager.ts:746 safeParse). Server: sites.service.ts:532 types the same column as `Array<{ fromSlug, toSlug, changedAt }>`. Three shapes, one column.
fix: Delete the editor-local PageDataSchema.slugHistory shape and the sites.service cast, and have both import SlugChange / slugHistorySchema from packages/shared/schemas/sites.ts — which is the one that matches what is actually written.
chain: Pages -> SlugChange -> written {slug,changedAt} -> validated as {slug,timestamp} in collaboration import, typed as {fromSlug,toSlug,changedAt} on the server -> any redirect generator built on the type reads undefined

finding: The pre-publish 'SEO configured' check does not look at a single page: it gates on the Site's metaTitleTemplate column, set on the dashboard, so a site where every page has a hand-written meta title fails the check and a site with a template and no page titles passes it.
evidence: publish.service.ts:33 selects `metaTitleTemplate` and :76 `if (!site?.metaTitleTemplate)` pushes the 'SEO configured' warning. The editor's per-page title lives at page.settings.seo.metaTitle (usePageSettings.ts:275) and is persisted into the Page.settings JSON column (sites.service.ts:683). The dedicated Page.seoTitle / Page.seoDescription columns (schema.prisma:585-586) are read by site-detail.service.ts:101 and site-settings.service.ts:111 but are NEVER written from the editor: saveProjectFromEditor maps `seoTitle: p.seoTitle ?? undefined` (sites.service.ts:526) from a PageData field that does not exist — PageData (types/project.ts:144-176) has no seoTitle. The template itself IS honoured at export (SEOInjector.ts:52-58 applyTitleTemplate).
fix: Make the check read the pages: warn when live pages are missing a meta title or description (page.settings.seo.metaTitle ?? Page.seoTitle), and keep the template as a separate, lower-severity note. Either write Page.seoTitle/seoDescription from the editor save or drop the two columns — right now the dashboard's SEO health reads a column the editor never fills.
chain: Pages -> PageSEO.metaTitle -> saved into Page.settings JSON -> runPrePublishChecks reads Site.metaTitleTemplate instead -> the SEO check answers a question about the site while claiming to describe the pages

finding: Page folders are a first-class organising device in the panel and exist only in one browser's localStorage — not in ProjectData, not on the server — so they vanish on a new device, are invisible to teammates, and are lost with site data clearing.
evidence: useFolders.ts:25-52: `STORAGE_KEY_PREFIX = 'pg-folders-v1-'`, `localStorage.getItem(storageKey(siteId))`; the module docstring at :4-6 states 'Folders are a UI organisational concept, NOT stored in the engine.' FolderItem is declared in pages/types.ts:15-20 and appears nowhere in shared/types/project.ts's ProjectData (:30-48). PagesTab.tsx:60 passes `getSiteIdFromUrl()` as the scope. Bulk 'Move to folder' (PagesTab.tsx:198-204) writes only to this store.
fix: Either move folders into ProjectData (a `folders` array beside pagesOrder, persisted through Page.meta or projectSettings) or say so on the surface — a one-line note in the folder affordance that folders are local to this browser. Silent per-device state on a collaborative product is the expensive kind of surprise.
chain: Pages -> FolderItem -> useFolders -> localStorage only -> a teammate or a second device sees a flat, unorganised page list with no explanation

finding: src/engine/routing/ is decorative: PageRouter is maintained on every page create/slug-change/delete, and its two lookup methods have zero callers — the export builds its own page->filename map, and the only read in the product is a display string that already has a fallback.
evidence: PageRouter.ts exposes register/unregister/resolve/getPath/getAllRoutes/clear. Grep across packages/editor/src (excluding engine/routing and tests): `router.resolve` — 0 hits; `getAllRoutes` — 0 hits outside its own definition; `router?.getPath?.` — one hit, usePages.ts:111-113, feeding PageItem.route, which is read once at SiteStructureTree.tsx:19 `(p.route ?? \`/${p.slug}\`)` — i.e. behind a fallback that makes it optional. ExportEngine.buildPageHrefs (:778-797) constructs its own map from slug + resolveHomePageId and never consults the router, contradicting PageManager.ts:7 ('composer.router — consumed by export, runtime routing').
fix: Either make the export resolve through the router (one map, one home-page rule, one place where a slug becomes a path) or delete PageRouter and the registerRoute/unregisterRoute/reregisterRoute wiring in PageManager. Two independent slug->path maps is the shape that lets them disagree.
chain: Pages -> PageRouter routes -> maintained on every mutation -> read by one fallback-covered label -> export invents a second, independent slug->filename map

finding: pagesOrder is in ProjectData, is written by exactly one line in the load path, is dropped by exportProject, and is read by nobody — page order actually survives on the `position` column derived from array index, which means the documented ordering field and the real one are different things.
evidence: types/project.ts:36 declares `pagesOrder?: string[]` ('drag-to-reorder source of truth'). The only writer is BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:295 `pagesOrder: sortedPages.map((p) => p.id)`. Composer.exportProject (:603-616) returns version/pages/styles/assets/metadata/settings and no pagesOrder, so it is gone on the first save. Real persistence: sites.service.ts:527 `position: index` over projectData.pages, and load re-sorts by position (BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:268-270). Reorder itself works — PageManager.reorderPage:337-357 rebuilds the Map and emits PROJECT_CHANGED 'page:reordered', which usePages.ts:139 syncs on.
fix: Delete pagesOrder from ProjectData and from the editor Zod schema (schemas/project.ts:36), or make exportProject emit it and the server honour it. Leaving a field named 'source of truth' that nothing reads is how the next person orders pages by the wrong key.
chain: Pages -> ProjectData.pagesOrder -> written on load only -> dropped by exportProject -> order in fact carried by Page.position; the declared ordering field is dead

finding: Deleting a page orphans every review comment pinned to it: Comment.pageId is a bare String with no relation and no FK, no delete path clears it, and the Review panel then renders the raw cuid as a group heading.
evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:471-497 — Comment has `pageId String?` and relations only to Site and Reviewer; there is no Page relation, so no cascade. server/services/page.service.ts:117-125 deletePage removes formBlock rows and the page, and nothing else. sites.service.ts:634-641 (the editor's full-snapshot path) deletes formBlocks for removed pages and the pages, and nothing else. listComments (comment.service.ts:50-53) filters by siteId only. ReviewTab.tsx:234-237 `pages.find((p) => p.id === pageId)?.name ?? pageId` — the fallback prints the id.
fix: Add the Page relation with onDelete: SetNull (or Cascade if a page's comments should die with it), and have the delete-confirm dialog name the count of open comments on that page before removing it. At minimum, group orphans under a real label instead of a cuid.
chain: Pages -> PageData -> deletePage -> (no comment cleanup, no FK) -> Review/Comments -> a client's open feedback survives as a row headed by a raw cuid, attached to a page nobody can open

finding: The per-plan page limit is unenforceable: the only place that checks pagesPerSite is page.service.createPage, and pages.create has no caller anywhere — the editor creates pages in engine memory and persists them through a full-snapshot upsert that counts nothing.
evidence: page.service.ts:60-67 reads PLAN_LIMITS[plan].pagesPerSite (lib/constants/plan-limits.ts:29/50/71 — 10/30/50) and throws PAGE_LIMIT. Grep for 'pages.create' across the repo (excluding the router/service that define it): zero hits. The editor path is PageManager.createPage (:61-92, no limit), exportProject, sites.saveProject -> saveProjectData (sites.service.ts:643-716), whose per-page upsert loop has no count check; it only writes `pages: input.pages.length` onto the Site row at :742.
fix: Enforce the limit at the write boundary that is actually used: count incoming pages in saveProjectData against PLAN_LIMITS and reject (or refuse only the excess) with a typed error, and have usePages.addPage read the plan (BuildrikSyncProvider already caches it as _editorPlanTier) so the panel can say no before the work is done.
chain: Pages -> PageData -> addPage -> sites.saveProject full snapshot -> saveProjectData upserts unbounded -> a FREE workspace ships 50 pages on a 10-page plan and the guard that exists is never reached

finding: Confirmed W-CO-02 from this module's side: pages.create/update/delete and all three translation procedures have no caller — every page mutation in the editor travels as part of one whole-project snapshot, which is why concurrent editing is all-or-nothing rather than per-page.
evidence: Callers of pages.list: BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:259 and packages/dashboard/app/onboarding/ai/preview/page.tsx:57. Callers of pages.create / pages.update / pages.delete / pages.setTranslation / pages.getTranslation / pages.removeTranslation: none (repo-wide grep excluding routers/pages.ts and page.service.ts returns only unrelated `ctx.pages.get/.delete` engine lines and tests). The editor path is Composer.exportProject -> BuildrikSyncProvider.saveProject:352-400 -> sites.saveProject -> saveProjectFromEditor:489-541 -> saveProjectData:593-748, which upserts every page and DELETES any page absent from the payload (:631-641).
fix: Keep the snapshot save as the content path, but delete the five unreachable procedures or wire the ones with a real job (translations). Meanwhile note the consequence in the intent docs: because a save is a whole-project replace, two people editing different pages of one site cannot both win — sites.service.ts:601-607 correctly rejects the second with SAVE_CONFLICT, so the answer to 'multi-device editing' is 'last loader wins, the other reloads'.
chain: Pages -> PageData -> editor mutations -> exportProject snapshot -> sites.saveProject (optimistic concurrency on Site.lastEditedAt) -> second device gets SAVE_CONFLICT for the whole project even when it touched a different page

finding: Page translations are a complete, tested server feature with no way in and no way out: no UI writes a translation, and the static deploy has no locale routing, so a locale enabled in the editor's Localization screen can never reach a visitor.
evidence: Server: page.service.ts:134-239 (resolveTranslation with a documented fallback chain, setTranslation, removeTranslation), Page.translations Json column (schema.prisma:591), full Zod schemas (packages/shared/schemas/pages.ts:33-55), a dedicated test file (server/services/__tests__/translation.test.ts). Editor: the only mention of the word is LocalizationScreen.tsx:6 ('set per-block in Phase B'). That screen writes only site.defaultLocale / enabledLocales. Deploy: ExportEngine.exportAllPages (:618-740) writes one file per page named from its slug (buildPageHrefs :778-797) with no locale segment, and lib/publish-files.ts:52-84 adds only robots.txt and sitemap.xml — there is no server at runtime to run resolveTranslation against.
fix: Either build the per-page locale editor and emit /<locale>/<page>.html variants at export (the sitemap and canonical builders in lib/publish-urls.ts would need locale awareness too), or hide the Localization screen behind the same 'not yet enforced' language the Advanced tab uses for password pages. Offering a locale switch that produces nothing is the same shape as the password setting that was silently ignored.
chain: Pages -> Page.translations -> full server API + Localization screen -> no writer, no locale-aware export -> an enabled locale changes nothing a visitor can see

finding: The Pages panel and the deploy disagree about the default state of a page: the panel labels a page with no visibility set 'Draft', while the exporter treats exactly that state as LIVE and ships it.
evidence: usePages.ts:120 `status: (p.settings?.visibility as PageItem['status']) ?? "draft"` (comment: 'A new page can't be Live before the project is published'). ExportEngine.ts:120-123 `isPageLive` returns true when `page.settings?.visibility === undefined`. Same predicate drives the publish page count (usePublishSnapshot.ts:172) and the pre-publish check's live filter (publish.service.ts:39-42, `v === undefined || v === 'live'`). PageSettings.visibility (types/project.ts:203) has no 'draft' member at all — the panel's own PageStatus union (pages/types.ts:9) invents it.
fix: Pick one meaning for 'visibility unset'. If unset means live (which is what ships), the row badge should say Live, or say nothing. If unset means draft, isPageLive must exclude it — and that changes what deploys, so it needs a migration for the pages that have relied on the current behaviour.
chain: Pages -> PageSettings.visibility -> unset -> panel badge says Draft, ExportEngine.isPageLive says live -> the user sees 'Draft' on a page that is publicly served

finding: The page-visibility control renders two contradictory sentences at the same time: one says hidden and password pages are left out of the deploy entirely, the next says a hidden page is 'reachable via direct URL' and a password page asks visitors for a password.
evidence: AdvancedTab.tsx:49-56 renders, when visibility !== 'live': 'Not published. Hidden pages are left out of the deploy, and static hosting cannot ask for a password — so a password page is left out too…'. AdvancedTab.tsx:57-61 then renders unconditionally: `{s.visibility === 'hidden' && 'Page is not linked in menus but reachable via direct URL.'}` and `{s.visibility === 'password' && 'Visitors must enter a password to view this page.'}`. Both blocks are in the DOM together for every non-live value. The first is the true one (ExportEngine.ts:658 filters non-live pages out of the deploy).
fix: Delete the two stale sentences at :59-60, or move them behind the same condition inverted. The honest copy already exists one block above it.
chain: Pages -> PageSettings.visibility -> AdvancedTab -> user reads 'left out of the deploy' and 'reachable via direct URL' in the same panel

finding: Internal page links are dead in Preview and in 'copy page HTML': the `#page:` scheme is resolved only inside ExportEngine, and the third head — the one behind Quick preview, the preview modal, view mode and copy-HTML — is assembled by Composer.exportHTML, which never resolves it.
evidence: Composer.exportHTML (:641-700) builds its document from `this.elements.toHTML(options)`; ElementManager.toHTML:273 delegates to HTMLParser.toHTML, and grep for 'href' or 'page:' in engine/elements/manager/HTMLParser.ts returns only two PROJECT_CHANGED emits — no href rewriting. resolveHref lives only at ExportEngine.ts:800-803 and is called only from ExportEngine's own writers (:1033). So a preview page ships `href="#page:page_abc"`, a fragment for an id that does not exist.
fix: Move resolveHref/buildPageHrefs onto a shared helper both writers call — the same fix the file's own comments describe having already been applied twice (once for the title precedence, once for the publish writer). Preview whose job is 'this is what visitors see' must navigate.
chain: Pages -> #page:<id> internal link -> Composer.exportHTML (preview / copy HTML) -> no resolution -> clicking an internal link in Preview appends a hash and goes nowhere

finding: Setting a new home page tells the user 'Your navigation menu may need updating manually' — and the product gives them nothing to update it with: there is no generated navigation, no reverse index of internal links, and no surface that lists which elements point at which page.
evidence: usePages.ts:305-309 toast text. PageManager.setHomePage:239-252 flips isHome across the Map and emits PROJECT_CHANGED 'page:home' — no route re-registration and no link rewrite. Nothing in the export builds a nav from pages: every getAllPages consumer (grep, 20 hits) is a panel, the exporter, media/template usage, or LinkSection's dropdown. resolveHomePageId (ExportEngine.ts:145-147) then makes the new home index.html, so every hand-built link written as `#page:<oldHome>` now resolves to a non-root filename while the site root serves a different page.
fix: Build the reverse index this module keeps needing (which pages/elements link to page X) and surface it in two places: the home-page change toast and the delete-confirm dialog. It is the same index MOD-B-01 needs, and MOD-A-20 filed the CMS version of the same gap.
chain: Pages -> isHome -> setHomePage -> emits page:home -> nothing rewrites links or nav -> the site root changes and every internal link keeps pointing where it did, with a toast telling the user to fix it by hand

finding: Switching pages never clears the selection, so the inspector keeps editing an element that is no longer on the canvas — and deleting a page removes its elements from the registry without clearing a selection that may point into them.
evidence: PageManager.setActivePage:225-235 sets the active id and emits PROJECT_CHANGED + PAGE_CHANGED; it does not touch composer.selection. The only PAGE_CHANGED listener is AquibraStudio.tsx:295, which only records the id for the Issues scope. Repo-wide `selection.clear()` callers: HistoryManager:536/548 (restore), RecoveryManager:156/230 (inactivity sweep), ElementCRUD:126 (element delete), defaultCommands:123/393, and canvas hooks reacting to user clicks — none on a page change. PageManager.deletePage:259-266 deletes the page's elements from ctx.elements with no selection call. Elements for every page are registered (importPage:362-373 calls buildElementTree for all), so the stale element remains resolvable and editable.
fix: Clear the selection in setActivePage (and in deletePage when the selected element belongs to the page being removed). One line in the engine, at the moment the invariant breaks — the same placement argument Composer.importProject:586-592 already makes for the active-page invariant.
chain: Pages -> active page -> setActivePage / deletePage -> (no selection reset) -> Inspector / canvas overlays -> style edits land on an element the user cannot see, or on one whose page was just deleted

finding: The Pages panel has no concept of a CMS-generated page — it cannot list them, mark the page that serves as their template, or open one — and the binding that produces them is a stored EXPORT FILENAME, so changing the template page's slug silently unbinds it.
evidence: appendDynamicPagesToPublish (cms.service.ts:226-241) selects collections where pageTemplatePath is not null and matches it against `pages.find((p) => p.path === col.pageTemplatePath)` — the path comes from ExportEngine.buildPageHrefs (:787-796), i.e. `<slug>.html`. Change the slug and the lookup misses; nothing warns. The Pages panel's page list is built solely from composer.elements.getAllPages() (usePages.ts:103) — no server call, no dynamic rows. Nothing in packages/editor sets pageTemplatePath (ContentViews.tsx:630-635 says so in its own comment; the panel only shows a warning that no template is bound). MOD-A-09/A-10/A-11 own the CMS side of this.
fix: Bind the template by page ID, not by filename, and show generated pages in the Pages tree as a read-only group under their template page ('Blog · 12 generated'), with the collection named. The Pages panel is where a user goes to ask 'what pages does my site have', and today it cannot answer that question for a CMS site.
chain: Pages -> PageData.slug -> slug change -> CmsCollection.pageTemplatePath (a filename) no longer matches -> publish emits zero dynamic pages, with no warning on either surface

finding: Nothing warns that deleting or hiding a published page will start returning 404 at a URL that is live right now: the deploy is a full file-set replace, so the page's file simply stops being uploaded on the next publish, with no redirect, no 410, and no mention in the publish confirmation.
evidence: Deploy file set is built from the payload only — lib/publish-files.ts:53-67 maps input.pages and adds robots.txt/sitemap.xml; there is no carry-over of previously deployed paths. ExportEngine.ts:658 drops non-live pages from that payload. runPrePublishChecks (publish.service.ts:18-107) has six checks — Vercel, Pages ready, SEO, Domain, Empty pages, Favicon — and none compares the outgoing page set against what is currently live. publish.service.ts:489-549 DOES compute added/removed/changed paths (PublishPageChange) but only for the post-hoc diff view.
fix: The removed-path computation already exists (publish.service.ts:546). Surface it before the publish, not after: 'about.html is live and is not in this publish — it will 404', with a one-click 'add a redirect' that writes a Redirect row. Same mechanism MOD-B-05 needs for slug changes.
chain: Pages -> PageData -> delete or set Hidden -> next publish uploads a file set without it -> the live URL 404s with no redirect and no pre-publish warning

finding: Three page events are declared, typed, commented — and are emitted by nothing and listened to by nothing: PAGE_CREATED, PAGE_TEMPLATE_ATTACHED, PAGE_TEMPLATE_DETACHED. Two other files carry comments warning the next reader not to trust them.
evidence: events.ts:474-475 declares the two template events with a rationale ('lets useTemplateUsageMap invalidate efficiently') and payload types at :890-891; grep for EVENTS.PAGE_TEMPLATE_ATTACHED / _DETACHED across packages/editor/src: zero hits outside that declaration. PageManager emits TEMPLATE_APPLIED / TEMPLATE_REMOVED instead (:196-199, :217-219). events.ts:487 PAGE_CREATED: the only two mentions are warnings — useAutoMilestone.ts:247-253 and OnboardingMount.tsx:82 both say the real signal is PROJECT_CHANGED's `page:created` type.
fix: Delete the three constants and the two payload type rows. A declared event with a docstring is indistinguishable from a working one until someone subscribes to it and waits.
chain: Pages -> PAGE_CREATED / PAGE_TEMPLATE_ATTACHED / PAGE_TEMPLATE_DETACHED -> no emitter, no listener -> the next consumer subscribes to the documented name and silently receives nothing

finding: Duplicating a page drops its applied-template history, so the copy loses the applied-template badge and any future version pinning that meta was persisted for.
evidence: PageManager.duplicatePage:312-323 constructs the copy with id/name/slug/isHome/root/settings/styles/updatedAt/slugManuallySet/slugHistory — no `meta`. PageMeta.appliedTemplates (types/project.ts:126-133) is the field recordAppliedTemplate (:196) writes and the templates panel reads (useTemplateUsageMap / templateUsage.ts:32). The field is explicitly persisted for this reason (sites.service.ts:654, 'REGRESSION-1: applied-template state survives reload').
fix: Carry `meta: source.meta ? JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(source.meta)) : undefined` in the duplicate, the same deep copy settings already gets at :318.
chain: Pages -> PageMeta.appliedTemplates -> duplicatePage -> meta not copied -> Templates panel shows the copy as using no template

finding: 'Copy link' refuses to give a URL for a site that is live, because it asks only about a custom domain and never about the published URL the same module already reads two files away.
evidence: usePages.copyPageLink:334-345 reads `composer?.getProjectMetadata?.()?.domain` and, when null, toasts 'No address yet — Connect a custom domain in Settings, or publish the site first.' ProjectMetadata also carries publishedUrl (types/project.ts:75), loaded at BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:335 and used by usePageSettings.ts:361 for exactly this 'is the site reachable' question. So a site published to a *.vercel.app URL with no custom domain gets told to publish.
fix: Fall back to publishedUrl when domain is unset: `const base = domain ? \`https://${domain}\` : publishedUrl`. Keep the toast for the genuinely unreachable case.
chain: Pages -> PageData.slug -> copyPageLink -> reads metadata.domain only -> a published site with no custom domain is told to publish

finding: Six PageSEO fields the exporter emits have no input anywhere in the product: canonicalUrl, structuredData, twitterCard, twitterTitle, twitterDescription, twitterImage.
evidence: PageSEO (types/project.ts:205-231) declares all six; SEOInjector.inject reads page.settings.seo and emits them. The Page settings drawer collects exactly eleven values (usePageSettings.ts:81-93 PersistedState): seoTitle, seoDesc, slug, ogTitle, ogDesc, ogImageUrl, visibility, password, allowIndex, allowFollow, customHead — and the save at :265-282 writes only metaTitle/metaDescription/ogTitle/ogDescription/ogImage/noIndex/noFollow. No tab renders a canonical, structured-data or Twitter field (grep of SeoTab/SocialTab/AdvancedTab for Label htmlFor: eight fields total). W-F-17 already filed the board's canonical field having no producer.
fix: Either add the fields (canonical and structured data are the two that change search behaviour) or delete them from PageSEO so the type stops describing a product that does not exist. Twitter falls back to og:* in the injector, so it is the cheapest to drop.
chain: Pages -> PageSEO.canonicalUrl / structuredData / twitter* -> no input in any tab -> the exporter's support for them can never be exercised

finding: The Pages panel's status vocabulary is four sizes larger than the field behind it, and one branch guards on a value that can never occur.
evidence: pages/types.ts:9 PageStatus = live | draft | hidden | password | scheduled | error | external. PageSettings.visibility (types/project.ts:203) = live | hidden | password. usePages.ts:120 casts visibility straight into PageStatus with a 'draft' default, so scheduled/error/external have no writer at all — and usePages.setHomepage:293-300 branches on `page?.status === 'external'` to refuse setting an external-link page as the homepage, a refusal that can never fire.
fix: Narrow PageStatus to the three real values plus whatever the panel genuinely derives (a 'draft' pseudo-state, if MOD-B-16 is resolved that way) and delete the external-link guard with it.
chain: Pages -> PageStatus -> four members with no writer -> a guard in setHomepage that is unreachable and a badge vocabulary that promises states the product does not have

finding: The shared sidebar test mock emits page event payload types the engine never emits, so every Pages test that drives it is exercising a vocabulary that does not exist in the product.
evidence: mockComposer.ts:86/91/99/105/110/116 emit PROJECT_CHANGED with types 'page:activate', 'page:add', 'page:duplicate', 'page:delete', 'page:update', 'page:home'. PageManager emits 'page:activated' (:227), 'page:created' (:89, :330), 'page:updated' (:172), 'page:deleted' (:275), 'page:reordered' (:355), 'page:home' (:249); HTMLParser adds 'page:imported' (:103). Only 'page:home' matches. It survives today because usePages.ts:139 filters on the `page:` prefix — a consumer that filtered on an exact type would pass its tests and fail in the app.
fix: Have the mock emit the engine's own strings. Better, export the payload-type union from PageManager and have both the mock and the filters use it, the way isNavigationOnlyChange (events.ts:695) already does for one of them.
chain: Pages -> PROJECT_CHANGED payload types -> mockComposer emits six names the engine never emits -> a test-green consumer that filters by exact type would be dead in the product
